CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 35 years
Gestation: 17 weeks
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age screening for chromosomal abnormalities
Previous Testing: Rapid PCR analysis performed

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis (Karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured using standard in situ culture techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells from at least two independent cultures were analyzed at a resolution of approximately 450-550 bands per haploid set.

RESULTS

Karyotype: 46,XX

INTERPRETATION
Normal female karyotype.

No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other numerical chromosomal abnormalities detected.
No major structural chromosomal rearrangements identified within the resolution limits of this analysis.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This analysis is sufficient to exclude numerical abnormalities and major structural rearrangements. However, the following limitations apply:
- Small deletions or duplications (<5-10 Mb) may not be detected
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
- Balanced rearrangements without phenotypic effect may not be detected
- Single gene disorders cannot be excluded by this test
- Uniparental disomy cannot be detected by standard karyotyping

CLINICAL CORRELATION
This normal female karyotype result indicates the absence of detectable chromosomal abnormalities within the resolution limits of conventional cytogenetic analysis. The risk for Down syndrome and other major chromosomal abnormalities is significantly reduced but not eliminated.

This result supersedes the rapid PCR analysis previously performed on this specimen.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results in the context of the pregnancy
2. Routine prenatal care should continue
3. If ultrasound abnormalities are detected later in pregnancy, additional testing such as chromosomal microarray analysis may be considered
4. No further cytogenetic testing is indicated based on current findings

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
